DocsHome.title: Connex documentation
DocsHome.lead: Connex is a relationship-intelligence CRM: it scores how warm each relationship is, predicts when one is cooling, and surfaces the warmest path to any introduction. These docs walk every capability, from the big fundamentals down to the small interface details.

DocsGettingStarted.title: Getting started
DocsGettingStarted.description: What Connex is, how workspaces and tenancy work, and how to find your way around.
DocsGettingStarted.lead: Start here. These pages cover the mental model behind Connex and the fundamentals every other section builds on.

what-is-connex.title: What is Connex
what-is-connex.description: The relationship-intelligence CRM and the ideas that make it different.

text: Connex is a multi-tenant CRM built around one idea: your relationships have a temperature, and that temperature changes over time. Instead of a static list of contacts, Connex continuously scores how warm each relationship is, warns you when one is cooling, and shows you the warmest path to reach anyone.
Everything in the product is tenant-scoped and permission-aware. What you see, edit, and share is always bounded by your workspace and your role within it.

workspaces-and-tenancy.title: Workspaces and tenancy
workspaces-and-tenancy.description: How multi-tenant isolation, workspace switching, and membership work.

blocks.text: A workspace is your tenant. Every record, file, tag, and setting belongs to exactly one workspace, and Connex enforces that boundary on every request. You can belong to more than one workspace and switch between them without logging out.

items.title: Open the workspace switcher
items.description: It sits at the top of the sidebar, showing your current workspace.

items.title: Pick another workspace
items.description: Your active tenant changes immediately and the whole app re-scopes to it.

items.title: Stay oriented
items.description: Your selection is remembered, so you land back in the same workspace next time.

blocks.title: Isolation is absolute
blocks.body: Data never crosses workspaces. An invitation or a shared record is the only way someone in another tenant sees anything you own.

navigating-connex.title: Navigating Connex
navigating-connex.description: The sidebar, global search, breadcrumbs, and how the app is laid out.

blocks.text: The left sidebar groups the app into Overview, Records, Activity, Library, and Team. The header carries global search and your workspace context. Most detail pages offer a back button to their list.

items.action: Dismiss the open menu or dialog

items.question: Is my data shared across workspaces?
items.answer: No. Every record is scoped to one workspace and never leaks to another tenant.

items.question: Do I need to score relationships manually?
items.answer: No. Warmth is computed automatically from the signals Connex already tracks.

warmth-and-temperature.title: Warmth & temperature
warmth-and-temperature.description: How relationship temperature is scored and what the bands mean.

blocks.text: Every relationship in Connex carries a temperature. It rises with recent, frequent, meaningful contact and falls as interactions thin out. The score rolls up into four readable bands so you can scan a list and know where each relationship stands.

items.label: Hot
items.description: Active, frequent, recent contact. The relationship is thriving.

items.label: Warm
items.description: Healthy and current, with steady but less frequent touchpoints.

items.label: Cool
items.description: Fading. Contact has slowed and the relationship needs attention.

items.label: Cold
items.description: Dormant. Little or no recent interaction to draw on.

blocks.title: Scores are computed, not entered
blocks.body: You never set a temperature by hand. It is derived from the signals Connex already tracks: notes, activities, meetings, and messages.

decay-and-signals.title: Decay & signals
decay-and-signals.description: How Connex predicts cooling relationships and what feeds the score.

blocks.text: Warmth decays over time. Connex models that decay and flags relationships that are about to slip a band, so you can reach out before they cool. The dashboard surfaces these as cooling relationships.
